chunks: And by this chain of narration, from (Al-Hasan ibn) Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) gave me a rose with both of his hands. When I brought it close to my nose, he said: 'It is the master of the fragrant flowers of Paradise after the myrtle.'
ai.seo_question: What is the status of the rose in Paradise according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the spiritual intimacy between the Prophet and Imam Ali, emphasizing the rose's status as a symbol of divine favor and purity in Shia tradition. The specific ranking of the rose after the myrtle (al-as) underscores the botanical hierarchy of Paradise, linking physical fragrance to spiritual nobility. This tradition serves as a metaphor for the 'sweetness' of faith and the blessed nature of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-128 According to the same documentation, it is narrated that (Al-Hassan ibn) Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) said,
“God’s Prophet (S) gave me a red rose with his own blessed hands. When I brought it close to my nose, he (a.s.) said, “After the leaves of the myrtle, this red rose is the best flower in Paradise.”
